about: Part A: planted defects. Each draft is a known base PRD with one edit. Seeded edits plant a defect the code gates cannot see; clean edits are harmless rewording. A reviewer detects a case when its critique names the planted defect. H cases are harder: buried, distant, off-by-one or implied. Clean controls use only the hand-checked recorded PRD, because the real run's synthesis carries a real flaw both reviewers found.

cases.notice: AC-32 calls a deadline 15 days away urgent. Urgent is 14 days or fewer, so 15 days is soon.
AC-13 says the deadline is 2026-11-28, but the date of service 2026-08-20 plus 90 days is 2026-11-18.

edits.find: 2026-11-18, which is the date of service plus 90 days
edits.replace: 2026-11-28, which is the date of service plus 90 days

cases.notice: REQ-12 lets the PFS lead override the gate, contradicting REQ-3 (nobody may override) and the agreed answer 'Nobody in v1'.

edits.find: None of these roles has a ready action or an override.
edits.replace: None of these roles has a ready action, except that the PFS lead may override the gate with a written justification.

cases.notice: REQ-1 applies the gate to every denial class, but the agreed answer was CO-50 only, and the rest of the document assumes CO-50 only.

edits.find: The readiness gate applies only to CO-50 denial lines. CO-16, CO-197, CO-4, PR-1, and OA-23 keep their current paths and are never gated.
edits.replace: The readiness gate applies to every denial class: CO-50, CO-16, CO-197, and CO-4. PR-1 and OA-23 keep their current paths and are never gated.

cases.notice: REQ-8 gives PR-1 lines an appeal action, but PR-1's only allowed action is to post the amount to patient responsibility and not open an appeal.

edits.find: An unknown code stays unmapped with no invented meaning and no gate.
edits.replace: An unknown code stays unmapped with no invented meaning and no gate. PR-1 lines offer an appeal action so the specialist can contest the deductible.

cases.notice: AC-8's outcome is a feeling ('easy to understand', 'feels confident'), so no test can observe whether it passed.

edits.find: Line A's control is enabled and line A becomes appeal-ready, while line B's control stays disabled naming the clinical-note reference and line B stays in denied.
edits.replace: The specialist finds the two-line claim easy to understand and feels confident about which line is ready.

cases.notice: AC-5 uses a real-looking patient name and street address. Only synthetic PAT-, CLM- and DOC- ids are allowed.

edits.replace: CLM-221 for Maria Alvarez of 1420 Elm Street, Springfield

cases.notice: REQ-12 lets the front desk mark a packet ready, contradicting its own first sentence (only the denial specialist may) and the roles policy.

edits.find: The front desk has no denial workqueue route at all;
edits.replace: The front desk may mark a CO-50 packet ready when no specialist is available;

cases.notice: REQ-9 now has the product suggest a corrected diagnosis code on CO-50 denials. The CO-50 rule says not to change the diagnosis code in this product, and the out-of-scope list forbids suggesting one.

edits.find: The product offers no control that decides medical necessity, changes or suggests a diagnosis or procedure code, invents a modifier, or writes off a balance, in any state before or after the gate.
edits.replace: The product offers no control that decides medical necessity, invents a modifier, or writes off a balance. On a CO-50 denial it suggests a corrected diagnosis code to strengthen the appeal.

cases.notice: The Q-4 assumption says the deadline is the date of service plus 180 days. The payer rule, and the agreed answer, say 90 days.

edits.replace: date of service plus 180 days, per Northwind Health's timely-filing rule

cases.notice: New REQ-5 requires a clinical-note reference on CO-16 denials, contradicting REQ-2 (CO-16 is unchanged) and AC-4.

append.statement: CO-16 denials also need a clinical-note reference before they can be marked ready.
append.rationale: Keeps the checklist the same across denial codes.

append.given: A CO-16 denial with no clinical-note reference
append.then: The packet stays not ready and names the clinical-note reference

cases.notice: AC-2 marks the packet ready when the deadline is missing, contradicting REQ-1 (both items must be present).

edits.find: The packet stays not ready and the missing item is the filing deadline
edits.replace: The packet becomes ready, because a missing deadline is filled in as 90 days from today

cases.notice: AC-31 gives CLM-303 a deadline of 2027-01-07, which is 51 days after the demo clock (comfortable), yet the same criterion calls it soon and sorts it before the comfortable row.
The out-of-scope list now excludes disabling the ready control while the gate fails, but REQ-6 requires exactly that.

edits.append: Disabling the ready control while the gate fails; v1 shows a warning beside an enabled control instead

cases.notice: REQ-11 makes urgent run through 15 days and soon start at 16, but the payer rule (and AC-32) put 15 days in soon.

edits.find: urgent from 0 through 14 days inclusive, soon from 15 through 45 days inclusive
edits.replace: urgent from 0 through 15 days inclusive, soon from 16 through 45 days inclusive

cases.notice: AC-13 says 3 days remain, but the deadline 2026-11-18 is 1 day after the demo clock of 17 November 2026.
AC-5 gives PAT-221 a birth date (born 1961-04-09). A date of birth is patient data even when it is not labelled DOB.
REQ-12 lets the coder enter a missing clinical-note reference, which changes a gate item; only the denial specialist works the gate, and the coder owns modifiers and diagnosis pointers.

edits.find: the coder may open denial detail read-only from the coding queue;
edits.replace: the coder may open denial detail from the coding queue and enter a missing clinical-note reference;

cases.notice: No planted defect; REQ-3 is reworded without changing its meaning.

edits.find: PR-1 and OA-23 cannot be marked appeal-ready.
edits.replace: Neither PR-1 nor OA-23 can be marked appeal-ready.

cases.notice: No planted defect.
No planted defect; AC-5 is reworded without changing its meaning.
No planted defect; REQ-4 is reworded without changing its meaning.

edits.find: When the gate blocks, the specialist sees the names of the missing items.
edits.replace: When the gate blocks, the specialist is shown the names of the missing items.
